REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The 85 is Taurus's five-shot .38 Special on the small frame, and it is covered inside the big REVOLVERS book - one manual carrying roughly 67 models at once. Unlike some guns in that book, the 85 is named outright: in the small-frame specification table, in the +P list and in the exploded view. Hold on to one thing throughout: a procedure printed under another model's heading does not apply to your 85 because it is on the same page. Taurus publishes no disassembly for it - the cylinder swings out, and that is the whole field strip.

steps.title: Find your 85 in the book's own table first
steps.action: The 85 sits in the SMALL FRAME FIXED SIGHTS REVOLVERS table: .38 Special, DA/SA, five rounds. The 85 and 85 Ti come in 2-inch or 3-inch barrels; the 85 UL and 85 UL/Ti are 2-inch only.
steps.prose: One book, sixty-odd revolvers, six specification tables. Reading the wrong row is a real risk here: the 605 a few lines up the same table is a .357 Magnum, and the 650 and 850 just below are double-action-only guns. The caliber stamped on your barrel is the authority - on an 85 it is .38 Special, and nothing longer goes in the chambers.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Small Frame Fixed Sights Revolvers - specifications, printed p.12 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Thumb piece forward - and the 85 is NOT on the front-latch list
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and press the cylinder out to the left at the same time. The book lists exactly which models also need a front latch pressed - Models 30, 218, 416, 454, 444, 45, 513 and 513UL - and the 85 is not among them.
steps.prose: Forward is the whole trick, and it is where owners coming off other makes come unstuck: pressing the thumb piece down or inward simply pins the cylinder shut. On an 85 one latch is all there is. If the cylinder resists, the hammer is not fully down or a case rim is caught under the star - pressing harder on a second latch that is not there will only bend something.
steps.quote: LOADING THE CYLINDER FOR .357 MAGNUM / .38 SPECIAL With the thumb of the right hand, push the thumb piece forward and at the same time press the cylinder, swinging it out to the left. ATTENTION: On Model 30, Model 218, Model 416, Model 454, Model 444, Model 45, Model 513 and Model 513UL using the left thumb, press down the front latch simultaneously.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Muzzle up, one sharp push, five chambers
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. All five cases lift together on the star; confirm every one has left the cylinder.
steps.prose: A 2-inch 85 has a short ejector rod, and it does not give a full case length of travel - a half-hearted push can leave a case standing proud that drops back as the star returns. Muzzle up and one decisive stroke; if a case still sticks, a rod from the muzzle is the answer, not more force on the extractor.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: The 85 is on Taurus's +P list - by name
steps.action: Taurus allows SAAMI-rated +P ammunition only in the models it names for +P use, and the 85 is the first line of that list. That is a permission, not a recommendation: the same page asks you not to use +P unless you need it, particularly for practice.
steps.prose: This matters at the bench because +P is what wears a small-frame revolver - it loosens the cylinder's timing and cuts the forcing cone faster. Never +P+, in any Taurus. If your 85 is a titanium model, the book's titanium section adds that +P lead-bullet loads are not recommended: a light crimp can let a bullet creep forward and block the cylinder.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Nothing here transfers to a look-alike
steps.action: Take this guide as belonging to the 85 designations the book names, and nowhere else. Taurus prints the warning: look-alike firearms differ widely in the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: The 85 shares an exploded view with sixteen other Taurus designations, and it shares a silhouette with many small five-shot revolvers from other makers whose cylinder latches move the other way. If pushing the latch toward the muzzle does nothing, stop - you are not holding a Taurus 85.
steps.aside: The book's own exploded view for this family is headed: Models: 17C, 17 C UL, 410 PD, 605, 905, 73, 731, 731 UL, 85 RB, 85 85ti, 85 UL, 85 UL/Ti, 650, 850, 850 UL/Ti, 651, 851.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Cylinder out, five chambers looked into and felt
steps.action: Before any solvent comes out: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber. That is the working state for the entire clean.
steps.prose: Both senses. A brass case head deep in a chamber reads as chamber wall to the eye at bench-light angles, and a fingertip finds what the light hides. Five chambers is a small count - go round once in one direction and stop where you started.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the barrel stays on
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, five chambers empty. That is the whole 85 field strip. Taurus states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly, and then says plainly: do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.prose: Where a revolver needs opening for repair, the book routes it to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. On the titanium models it is firmer still: the barrel is a steel liner inside a titanium shroud, and trying to unscrew it damages the frame or the barrel. The exploded view at the back is a parts list, not a disassembly procedure.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Powder residue out of the barrel, lead scrubbed wet
steps.action: After shooting, remove all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush. If you find lead particles in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched in oil, then lubricate.
steps.prose: Wet brass brush, never steel and never dry. .38 Special practice loads are usually cast lead, and a 2-inch barrel is almost all forcing cone and first inches of rifling - exactly where lead strips off and stays. Work those hardest, then check the bore against a light.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, it is of special importance that all residues of powder be removed from barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, using an appropriate brush. If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Clean before further shooting past 200 rounds
steps.action: Brush all five chambers full length and clean the cylinder face and the area behind the star. The book adds that after more than 200 rounds in a row the firearm should be cleaned before further shooting.
steps.prose: A carbon ring builds on the cylinder face and is what eventually stops the cylinder closing; grit under the star holds it proud and the cylinder will not latch on it. A case that sticks on the next range trip usually started as residue left in the chamber on this one.
steps.quote: Once cleaned, lubrication should be done as above described. When shooting more than 200 rounds in a row, your firearm should be cleaned before further shooting.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: On a titanium 85: nothing abrasive, anywhere
steps.action: If your 85 is a titanium model (the Ti designations), never use an abrasive to clean the front face of the cylinder or any other part. Normal cleaning is fine; abrasives are not.
steps.prose: The cylinder's finish on these guns is a protective layer, not decoration - scrubbing the carbon ring off with an abrasive pad or a lead-removing cloth takes the finish with it and shortens the life of the cylinder. Solvent and patience on the face instead. On a steel 85 an abrasive is still bad practice; on a titanium one Taurus forbids it.
steps.quote: under no circumstances should you use any abrasive material to clean the front face of the cylinder, or any other part of the revolver, as the use of such an abrasive material can remove the finish on the cylinder, which is a protective layer, and this can greatly reduce the service life of the cylinder and the revolver.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Taurus Total Titanium and Ultralite Titanium Models, printed p.41 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: A lightly oiled cloth, a thin film, the crevices brushed
steps.action: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and do the same through the bore. Remove the excess oil but leave a thin protecting film, and brush the dust out of every crevice with a small, clean brush.
steps.prose: Thin is the word that matters: oil left pooled in the frame and under the crane collects grit and burnt residue. An 85 is often a carry gun, so store it away from anything that holds moisture, cloth holsters included.
steps.quote: 4. For normal cleaning of firearm not used or kept in storage for some time, it is necessary to rub it with a lightly oiled cloth. In the same way proceed with the bore of the barrel. The barrel should be clean and left free of debris. The excess oil must be removed, but a thin protecting film should remain. Also the dust should be removed from all crevices with a small, clean brush.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus REVOLVERS book publishes no disassembly for any model it covers. Its care section (printed p.40) opens by saying the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly, adds 'Do not disassemble the barrel.', and routes any necessary disassembly to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. Its titanium section (printed p.41) tells owners of those models not to try to unscrew the barrel and to return the revolver to Customer Service if service is required. The exploded views at the back are parts diagrams headed with model lists and carry no order of operations. Nothing deeper is walked because nothing deeper is published.

cleaning.name: BORE & FORCING CONE
tasks: Remove all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush
If lead particles are found in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched in oil, then lubricate
Work the forcing cone and the first inches of rifling hardest - on a short barrel that is where lead stays
Check the bore against a light before the revolver goes away

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & CHAMBERS
tasks: Brush all five chambers full length and follow with a dry patch
Take the carbon ring off the front face of the cylinder
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under it holds the star proud
Wipe the crane and the frame window
Never use an abrasive on the cylinder face or anywhere else on a titanium model

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, OIL & STORAGE
tasks: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and do the same through the bore; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush
Keep the revolver away from materials that attract moisture or carry acidity, and avoid cloth holsters that hold damp
For long storage take extra care to protect the metal surfaces against corrosion

reassembly: Nothing was removed, so nothing is refitted. Let the extractor rod return fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently until it latches - never flick it shut, which knocks a small-frame crane out of true and starts the cylinder binding.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and feel the cylinder stop drop into each of the five notches.
fncheck: With all five chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch under light thumb pressure with no perceptible side play; hand rotation should feel the cylinder stop engage at each notch; the hammer should hold at full cock without following; and both single and double action should reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Taurus's standing advice for its revolvers is to keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing.
